A.summary: Unfinished: 120 unconnected items (54 nets in pieces) including VBUS and VBATT to the charger, P2.5V to the FPGA, the DDR3 clock, USB D+ and the flash clock. Buck switch nodes are 0.089 mm tracks, the In1 ground plane covers only 38% under the FPGA, and it needs 75 laser microvias.

B.summary: Complete, through-vias only, two unbroken ground planes, DDR3 length-matched to about 0.5 mm with 2 vias per net, coupled USB pair, pours at the regulators. Needs clean-up (planes 0.15 mm from the edge, 0.10 mm NPTH clearance, duplicate B.Cu zone, zone refill hangs in KiCad 10) and a stackup decision because In2 crosses 108 power-island splits on In3.

C.summary: Sound stackup, real power islands, very tight decoupling and standard vias, but 29 nets are unrouted including USB D-, JTAG TCK/TMS, FPGA_RESET, SD clock and a USB-C CC resistor, so the board cannot be programmed. DDR3 is unmatched and tracks in the In3 ground plane cut slots under the In2 bus.

D.summary: Fully connected and DRC-clean with good USB and DQS pairs, but it relies on 499 blind, buried and micro vias with 115 stacked sites, which is a 2nd-order HDI build and not a standard 6-layer order. DDR3 is unmatched with up to 10 vias per net, the ground plane is perforated under the FPGA, and the DDR supply runs partly on 0.127 mm tracks.

human_guess.why: B has serpentine length tuning to a 15.0 mm target, thousands of sub-0.05 mm segment fragments from interactive routing, hand-drawn power islands with ad-hoc priorities, per-regulator pours, keepout areas, a duplicated zone and rounding-level DRC leftovers from older KiCad versions. A, C and D show tool-like regularity: uniform fan-out stubs including on unconnected pins (A), grid-regular vias in capacitor pads and unmatched straight buses (C), and a single track width with programmatic stacked-via ladders and a custom DRC rule (D).
